title: Hosted canary rollout wizard (Console): create rollout flow for traffic split + guardrails + review/confirm
creator: Tessa Morgan
content:
## Summary
Design the end-to-end “Hosted canary rollout” creation wizard in Redwood Console.

This wizard is the primary GA workflow for customers to safely introduce a new model version/config on a Hosted route using percentage-based traffic splitting (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%), with policy guardrails, approvals, and clear rollback implications.

Owners:
- Design: Kenji Nakamura (IC), Tessa Morgan (lead)
- Product: Marissa Cole
- Eng partners: Dylan Brooks (Console), Chloe Martin (Console backend), Ethan Park (control plane), Jordan Lee (policy engine)

Primary artifact links (internal):
- Design spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json
- Policy guardrails requirements (Linear): PM-1851
- Wizard backend contract PR (GitHub): pr-28863-console-rollouts-ui-wizard-backend-contracts


## Problem
Customers want to roll out a new Hosted route configuration with minimized blast radius and quick rollback. Current capabilities exist (model versioning, fallback routing), but there is no cohesive, guided workflow for percentage-based canaries that (a) makes the plan explicit, (b) prevents unsafe actions via policy, and (c) makes approvals/stop conditions comprehensible.

Design goals:
1) Reduce “misconfiguration” risk (wrong baseline/canary, unsafe jumps, missing soak time).
2) Make the plan legible (what traffic will go where, when, and under what stop conditions).
3) Make guardrails feel helpful, not punitive (clear error messages + suggested fix).
4) Make risky actions explicit (start rollout, increase canary %, rollback).

Non-goals (for this ticket):
- Building the detailed metrics comparison UI (see DES-763).
- Designing the timeline/activity panel beyond entry points/placement (see DES-755).


## Entry points
- Hosted Routes → Route details → “Rollouts” tab → “Create canary rollout”
- Model versions page (secondary) → “Roll out on route…” (deferred; not GA blocker)


## Wizard: steps + behavior
### Step 0: Preconditions / eligibility check
Shown before entering wizard if tenant/route is not eligible.
- Conditions to detect:
  - Feature flag not enabled for tenant
  - Route is not Hosted (Dedicated/Private)
  - Route has no baseline model version pinned (or baseline not resolvable)
- UX:
  - Blocking state with remediation steps + link to docs
  - “Contact support” CTA if tenant expects access

Copy guidance:
- Keep it factual; avoid implying blame.


### Step 1: Select route
Fields:
- Route picker (search + filter by environment if applicable)
- Read-only route context: current pinned model version/config, region policy summary, fallback policy summary

Validations:
- If route already has an active rollout → block and link to that rollout
- If route has recent config drift in last X minutes (control plane eventual consistency) → show warning, allow continue

Notes:
- Provide a small “What is a canary rollout?” inline explainer (1–2 sentences) with “Learn more” link.


### Step 2: Choose baseline and canary
Goal: Make baseline explicit, make canary differences visible.

Fields:
- Baseline: defaults to current active config/model version on route (read-only by default; “change” requires explicit action)
- Canary: select target model version/config (from allowed compatible list)

Compatibility behavior:
- If user selects an incompatible canary (e.g., tool calling not supported, context window mismatch, region availability mismatch):
  - Block with policy/validation error, show plain-English reason
  - Provide a “View compatible options” action

Diff summary panel (right side):
- Model version
- Quantization profile / runtime profile (if applicable)
- Max tokens / context length
- Safety settings / structured output settings (if part of route config)

Open question resolved (2025-02-18):
- Diff panel is “best effort”; if certain fields are unknown, show “Not available” rather than blocking.


### Step 3: Traffic schedule (step plan)
Goal: Help users pick a safe schedule while still allowing power users to configure.

Schedule modes:
1) Recommended schedule (default)
   - Preset steps: 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%
   - Default soak time per step based on route tier (policy-provided)
2) Custom schedule
   - Table editor with rows: step %, minimum soak time
   - Add/remove steps

Guardrails surfaced here (policy-driven):
- Max step size (e.g., cannot jump > 25% without approval)
- Minimum soak time per step
- Maximum total duration (optional; if policy exists)

UX details:
- Each policy violation is shown inline in the table row with an “Explain” tooltip.
- Provide an “Auto-fix” suggestion when possible (e.g., “Increase soak time to 30m”).

Defaults:
- Start at 1% unless policy overrides.
- If route traffic volume is low (detected via telemetry hint), show suggestion: “Consider higher % or longer soak to get statistically useful signal.” (non-blocking)


### Step 4: Guardrails and stop conditions
Goal: Make safety controls understandable, and clarify what is automatic vs requires human action.

Sections:
A) Approvals
- Toggle/setting: “Require approval to increase canary above X%” (pre-filled by policy, editable only if user has permission)
- Show who can approve (based on RBAC): role names + link to access settings

B) Automatic stop / rollback (SLO-based)
- Enabled by default (if available for tenant)
- Display thresholds in human-readable terms:
  - Error rate increase vs baseline
  - p95 latency regression vs baseline
  - Timeout rate regression
- Each has:
  - Threshold value
  - Evaluation window
  - Action on breach: “Pause rollout” or “Rollback to baseline” (policy-controlled)

C) Notifications
- Channels: email + Slack (if integrated)
- “Notify on: step start, step complete, approval needed, auto-stop triggered, rollback completed”

D) Quality gates (GA scope)
- Copy: “Optional (beta): attach external evaluation result URL”
- This is non-blocking and does not auto-stop in GA.

Warning copy (from design review):
- Explicitly state that canary traffic receives real production requests.


### Step 5: Review and confirm
Goal: Prevent accidental rollout creation and make the plan auditable.

Review includes:
- Route
- Baseline + canary summary
- Schedule steps + soak times
- Approvals requirement
- Auto-stop settings
- “What happens if something goes wrong?”
  - Auto-stop behavior
  - Manual pause
  - Manual rollback

Confirmation pattern:
- Primary CTA: “Create rollout”
- Secondary: “Save as draft” (only if backend supports; otherwise remove)
- After create: landing page is rollout details view (timeline + metrics entry points).

Destructive-action confirmation:
- Not required at create time.
- Required later for “Rollback now” (outside wizard; tracked in DES-755/ENG-9140).


## Error + empty states (key ones)
- Policy denies action: show inline banner with clear reason and what to change.
- Backend validation mismatch: show banner “We couldn’t validate your plan” + retry; log correlation ID.
- Route has an active rollout: block with deep link.
- No compatible canary options: block, explain common causes (region availability, features), link to docs.


## Accessibility + i18n
- Wizard steps must be keyboard-navigable.
- Avoid relying on color for baseline vs canary.
- All charts are out of scope here; any visualizations in review must have textual equivalents.


## Analytics (instrumentation requests)
To help PM validate activation and drop-off:
- Wizard started
- Step completion events (step1/2/3/4/5)
- Validation errors encountered (policy vs backend)
- Rollout created successfully
- Save-as-draft used (if shipped)


## Deliverables
- Final Figma frames for:
  - Eligibility gate
  - Step 1–5
  - Primary errors/warnings
- Copy deck for warnings and confirmations
- Handoff notes to engineering (component usage, spacing, empty/error states)


## Open questions / decisions
1) Save as draft (resolved 2025-03-04): Defer for GA. Use “Create rollout” only. Engineering confirmed drafts would add state complexity; can be added post-GA.
2) Custom schedule granularity (resolved 2025-02-26): allow minutes/hours only; no seconds.
3) Approval UX (resolved 2025-03-06): Wizard config sets approval gates; actual approval UI is on rollout details page (DES-755).


## Acceptance criteria
- A user can complete wizard with default recommended schedule with minimal cognitive load.
- All policy errors are surfaced inline with actionable guidance.
- Review step makes baseline/canary and schedule unambiguous.
- Handoff includes all empty/error/warning states needed for GA.
comments: 2025-01-22 (Tessa Morgan): Kicking off DES-742. This is the GA-critical flow—please assume most users are cautious operators, not infra experts. Main risks: unclear baseline/canary selection + policy errors that read like “backend speak”.

2025-01-29 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafted initial step breakdown + early wireframes. Question for PM/Eng: do we support “save as draft” for Beta, or is create+pause the workaround? Also: do we default auto-stop to ON?

2025-02-03 (Marissa Cole): Default auto-stop ON where available. Drafts are nice-to-have but not required for GA; OK to defer if it adds orchestration complexity. Primary must-have is a crystal clear review/confirm step and a safe default schedule.

2025-02-07 (Dylan Brooks): Backend contract will include a validate/preview endpoint. Please design for server-returned validation messages with a field path (e.g., schedule[2].soak_time). We can map those to inline table errors.

2025-02-12 (Jordan Lee): Policy engine can return structured deny reasons + suggested remediation in some cases (e.g., min soak time). Don’t hardcode guardrail numbers in UI; treat them as policy-provided with fallbacks to “Not configurable for your org”.

2025-02-18 (Kenji Nakamura): Iteration 2: Added diff panel baseline vs canary, and explicit “Change baseline” action behind a secondary link. Included warning when route already has drift in the last few minutes (non-blocking).

2025-02-21 (Svetlana Orlov): Design system note: use existing Stepper + SidePanel summary patterns. For the schedule table, use the DataGrid component; inline validation is supported but avoid multi-line cells where possible.

2025-02-27 (Paula Mendes): Please ensure stop conditions are readable as “compared to baseline” (not absolute), since that’s how we’re evaluating in telemetry. Also note: quality gating is optional/manual for GA—no “hard gate” language.

2025-03-03 (Kenji Nakamura): Iteration 3: Guardrails step now has clear “Automatic stop/rollback” subsection, with action labels (Pause vs Rollback) and evaluation window. Added copy: “Canary traffic receives real production requests.”

2025-03-06 (Nora Ahmed): FYI for alignment with DES-755: approvals UI will live on rollout details; wizard only configures the gate. I’ll mirror the wording exactly (“Approval required to increase above X%”).

2025-03-10 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed draft-saving is not in backend scope for GA. Also confirmed we’ll return an eligibility error for unsupported routes/tenants; please design a pre-wizard blocking state with remediation instructions + support link.
2025-03-14 (Kenji Nakamura): Design review with PM + Eng: adjusted review step to include “What happens if something goes wrong?” and moved notifications to guardrails step (not schedule).

2025-03-19 (Tessa Morgan): Copy polish request based on Slack thread: destructive wording should be reserved for rollback; create/start should be framed as reversible with guardrails. Add a clear confirmation for leaving wizard with unsaved changes.

2025-03-26 (Kenji Nakamura): Marking complete. Final Figma + handoff notes sent to Dylan/Chloe; engineering confirmed mapping from validate endpoint errors to inline UI. Remaining work tracked in DES-755 (timeline/activity) + DES-763 (metrics comparison).
